scope: Genesis 42–45, all 134 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Genesis 42–45.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Renders saw as learned from the reported news and retains Jacob’s impatient question without inventing the sons’ motives.
verses.before: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you keep looking at one another?”
verses.after: When Jacob learned that grain was available in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just looking at one another?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you keep looking at one another?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated report and the live/not-die formula that Judah repeats in 43:8.
verses.before: And he said, “Look, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us from there, that we may live and not die.”
verses.after: “I have heard there is grain in Egypt,” he continued. “Go down there and buy some for us, so we can live and not die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us from there, that we may live and not die.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator’s Joseph-centered kinship description and the exact number traveling.
verses.before: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
verses.after: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to Egypt to buy grain.
verses.tsw_comparator: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the full brother from the traveling brothers and preserves Jacob’s feared disaster as his thought.
verses.before: Yet Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers, for he said, “Lest harm befall him.”
verses.after: But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with the others, because he thought, “Something terrible might happen to him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers, for he said, “Lest harm befall him.”

verses.rationale: Retains the Israel designation, wider movement of buyers, and Canaan’s famine as the reason for travel without adding a chronology of its spread.
verses.before: Thus the sons of Israel came to buy grain among people who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan also.
verses.after: Israel’s sons came to buy grain along with the others who were coming, for there was famine in Canaan too.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the sons of Israel came to buy grain among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan also.

verses.rationale: Keeps both political authority and grain distribution, followed by the bodily bow that recalls the dreams.
verses.before: Now Joseph was governor over the land. He was the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brothers came and bowed themselves before him with their faces to the ground.
verses.after: Joseph was the governor of the land, the one who sold grain to all its people. His brothers came and bowed before him with their faces to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Joseph was governor over the land. He was the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brothers came and bowed themselves before him with their faces to the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves recognizing/acting unrecognized as deliberate behavior rather than literal failure to know them.
verses.before: Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but he treated them as strangers and spoke harshly to them. He said to them, “Where do you come from?” They said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”
verses.after: Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but he acted like a stranger and spoke harshly to them. “Where have you come from?” he asked. “From Canaan, to buy food,” they answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but he treated them as strangers and spoke harshly to them. He said to them, “Where do you come from?” They said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”

verses.rationale: Retains the clear existing wording and the narrator’s repeated recognition contrast because it governs the scene.
verses.before: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
verses.after: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.

verses.rationale: Keeps remembered dreams and renders nakedness of the land as exposed vulnerability, with the Hebrew image disclosed in a note.
verses.before: Then Joseph remembered the dreams that he had dreamed about them. And he said to them, “You are spies. You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
verses.after: Joseph remembered the dreams he had dreamed about them. He said, “You are spies! You have come to see where the land lies exposed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joseph remembered the dreams that he had dreamed about them. And he said to them, “You are spies. You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”

verses.rationale: Retains respectful my lord/your servants language as deference, not a declaration of enslavement.
verses.before: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
verses.after: “No, my lord,” they answered. “Your servants have come to buy food.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.

verses.rationale: Preserves their argument from common parentage and the claim of honesty without endorsing it as narrator.
verses.before: We are all sons of one man. We are honest men. Your servants have never been spies.”
verses.after: We are all sons of one man. We are honest men; your servants have never been spies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: We are all sons of one man. We are honest men. Your servants have never been spies.”

verses.rationale: Repeats the accusation’s exact central phrase rather than varying it for style.
verses.before: But he said to them, “No, it is the nakedness of the land that you have come to see.”
verses.after: “No,” he said. “You have come to see where the land lies exposed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said to them, “No, it is the nakedness of the land that you have come to see.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the awkward twelve-member claim and renders one is not without deciding whether they mean dead or missing.
verses.before: They said, “We your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Look, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is no more.”
verses.after: They said, “Your servants are twelve brothers, sons of one man in Canaan. The youngest is with our father now, and one is no longer with us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “We your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is no more.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Joseph’s repeated accusation after their disclosure of the absent brothers.
verses.before: Yet Joseph said to them, “It is as I said to you: you are spies.
verses.after: Joseph replied, “It is just as I said: you are spies!
verses.tsw_comparator: But Joseph said to them, “It is as I said to you: you are spies.

verses.rationale: Retains the oath by Pharaoh’s life and the condition for release without changing its religious register.
verses.before: By this you will be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you will not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.after: Here is how you will be tested. As surely as Pharaoh lives, you will not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.

verses.rationale: Preserves the initial one-goes/rest-stay proposal, truth test, and repeated oath.
verses.before: Send one of you and let him bring your brother, while you remain confined, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you. Otherwise, by the life of Pharaoh, surely you are spies.”
verses.after: Send one of you to bring your brother, while the rest remain in custody. Your words will be tested to see whether you are telling the truth. If not, as surely as Pharaoh lives, you are spies!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Send one of you and let him bring your brother, while you remain confined, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you. Otherwise, by the life of Pharaoh, surely you are spies.”

verses.rationale: Keeps collective detention and its exact duration.
verses.before: And he put them all together in custody for three days.
verses.after: He put them all in custody for three days.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he put them all together in custody for three days.

verses.rationale: Preserves fear of God as Joseph’s own claim and keeps its connection to his revised terms.
verses.before: On the third day Joseph said to them, “Do this and live, for I fear God:
verses.after: On the third day Joseph said, “Do this, and you will live, for I fear God.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the third day Joseph said to them, “Do this and live, for I fear God:

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal from one traveler to one detainee and the families’ hunger as the purpose of release.
verses.before: if you are honest men, let one of your brothers remain confined in your prison, but the rest of you go and carry grain for the famine of your households.
verses.after: If you are honest men, let one brother remain here in custody. The rest of you may go and take grain home to your hungry households.
verses.tsw_comparator: if you are honest men, let one of your brothers remain confined in your prison, but the rest of you go and carry grain for the famine of your households.

verses.rationale: Renders the summary they did so prospectively in its narrative setting without suggesting Benjamin was already brought.
verses.before: Then bring your youngest brother to me, so your words will be verified, and you will not die.” And they did so.
verses.after: Then bring your youngest brother to me, so your words can be confirmed and you will not die.” They agreed to do this.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then bring your youngest brother to me, so your words will be verified, and you shall not die.” And they did so.

verses.rationale: Preserves guilt, Joseph’s previously unreported pleading, refused hearing, and the repeated anguish linking past and present.
verses.before: Then they said to one another, “Truly we are guilty concerning our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we would not listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”
verses.after: They said to one another, “We really are guilty because of what we did to our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen. That is why this anguish has come upon us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they said to one another, “Truly we are guilty concerning our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we would not listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Reuben’s recollection and the blood-accountability image without making the narrator pronounce Joseph dead.
verses.before: Reuben answered them, saying, “Did I not tell you, ‘Do not sin against the boy’? But you would not listen. And now an accounting for his blood is required.”
verses.after: Reuben answered, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen. Now we are being called to account for his blood.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Reuben answered them, saying, “Did I not tell you, ‘Do not sin against the boy’? But you would not listen. And now an accounting for his blood is required.”

verses.rationale: Renders hearing as comprehension while preserving the interpreter who enables their unguarded speech.
verses.before: They did not know that Joseph understood them, for an interpreter stood between them.
verses.after: They did not know that Joseph understood them, because an interpreter stood between them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They did not know that Joseph understood them, for an interpreter stood between them.

verses.rationale: Keeps grief and coercive detention together without explaining Joseph’s motive or choosing a reason for Simeon’s selection.
verses.before: Then he turned away from them and wept. Afterward he returned to them and spoke with them. And he took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.
verses.after: Joseph turned away from them and wept. Then he returned and spoke to them. He took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he turned away from them and wept. Afterward he returned to them and spoke with them. And he took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.

verses.rationale: Retains all three orders and their fulfillment; silver remains the ancient medium of exchange.
verses.before: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain and to return every man’s silver into his sack and to give them provisions for the journey. And it was done for them.
verses.after: Joseph ordered their bags filled with grain, each man’s silver returned to his sack, and provisions supplied for the journey. This was done for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain and to return every man’s silver into his sack and to give them provisions for the journey. And it was done for them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the grain, transport animals, and departure in concise narrative form.
verses.before: So they loaded their grain upon their donkeys and departed from there.
verses.after: They loaded the grain onto their donkeys and left.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they loaded their grain upon their donkeys and departed from there.

verses.rationale: Renders lodging place without imposing a commercial inn and retains the single discoverer and sack-mouth location.
verses.before: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey fodder at the lodging place, he saw his silver. And look, it was in the mouth of his sack.
verses.after: At the place where they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to feed his donkey and saw his silver there at the mouth of the sack.
verses.tsw_comparator: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey fodder at the lodging place, he saw his silver. And behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

verses.rationale: Keeps the heart idiom, shared fear, and their question about God as the characters’ interpretation.
verses.before: He said to his brothers, “My silver has been returned! And look, it is in my sack!” Then their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”
verses.after: “My silver has been returned!” he told his brothers. “Look, it is here in my sack!” Their hearts sank, and they turned to one another trembling. “What has God done to us?” they asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to his brothers, “My silver has been returned! And behold, it is in my sack!” Then their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”

verses.rationale: Introduces the full retelling without compressing the following dialogue.
verses.before: When they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan, they told him all that had happened to them, saying,
verses.after: When they reached their father Jacob in Canaan, they told him everything that had happened:
verses.tsw_comparator: When they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan, they told him all that had happened to them, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves their description of harsh treatment and the ruler’s unknown identity.
verses.before: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly to us and treated us as spies of the land.
verses.after: “The man who rules the land spoke harshly to us and treated us as spies.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly to us and treated us as spies of the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps their repeated self-description and nests their earlier speech clearly.
verses.before: But we said to him, ‘We are honest men. We have never been spies.
verses.after: We told him, ‘We are honest men. We have never been spies.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we said to him, ‘We are honest men. We have never been spies.

verses.rationale: Repeats the noncommittal absent-brother formula rather than silently making it an explicit death report.
verses.before: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is no more, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.’
verses.after: We are twelve brothers, sons of the same father. One is no longer with us, and the youngest is with our father in Canaan.’
verses.tsw_comparator: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is no more, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the reported version of Joseph’s conditions and clarifies the ellipsis take your households’ hunger.
verses.before: Then the man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, take grain for the famine of your households, and go.
verses.after: Then the man who rules the land said, ‘This is how I will know you are honest. Leave one brother with me, take grain for your hungry households, and go.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I shall know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, take grain for the famine of your households, and go.

verses.rationale: Keeps the promise of trade that appears in their retelling without inserting it into Joseph’s earlier speech.
verses.before: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies but honest men. I will return your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.’”
verses.after: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know you are honest men, not spies. I will give your brother back, and you may trade in the land.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I shall know that you are not spies but honest men. I will return your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the later discovery by all at home rather than harmonizing it with 43:21’s collective account at the lodging place.
verses.before: As they emptied their sacks, look, every man’s bundle of silver was in his sack. And when they and their father saw their bundles of silver, they were afraid.
verses.after: As they emptied their sacks, each man found his pouch of silver inside. When they and their father saw the pouches of silver, they were afraid.
verses.tsw_comparator: As they emptied their sacks, behold, every man’s bundle of silver was in his sack. And when they and their father saw their bundles of silver, they were afraid.

verses.rationale: Retains Jacob’s accusation, repeated absence formula, and self-focused grief without endorsing his account of Simeon’s fate.
verses.before: Jacob their father said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children. Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and now you would take Benjamin. All these things are against me.”
verses.after: Their father Jacob said, “You are robbing me of my children! Joseph is gone. Simeon is gone. Now you would take Benjamin. All of this falls on me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jacob their father said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children. Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and now you would take Benjamin. All these things are against me.”

verses.rationale: States the threatened killing of Reuben’s sons explicitly and distinguishes this pledge from Judah’s later personal guarantee.
verses.before: Then Reuben said to his father, “You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my hand, and I will return him to you.”
verses.after: Reuben said to his father, “You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring Benjamin back to you. Entrust him to me, and I will return him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Reuben said to his father, “You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my hand, and I will return him to you.”

verses.rationale: Retains Jacob’s selective only-son language, his explicit claim that Joseph is dead, and the gray-head/Sheol image.
verses.before: But he said, “My son will not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If harm should befall him on the journey that you are to make, then you would bring down my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol.”
verses.after: But Jacob said, “My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he alone is left. If disaster strikes him on your journey, you will bring my gray head down to Sheol in grief.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, “My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If harm should befall him on the journey that you are to make, then you would bring down my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol.”

verses.rationale: Retains the brief renewed statement of the crisis driving the second journey.
verses.before: Now the famine was severe in the land.
verses.after: The famine was severe in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the famine was severe in the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps exhausted provisions, repeat journey, and Jacob’s modest-sounding request.
verses.before: And when they had finished eating the grain that they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little food.”
verses.after: When they had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said, “Go back and buy us a little food.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And when they had finished eating the grain that they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little food.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic warning and face idiom that recurs through Judah’s later appeal.
verses.before: Yet Judah said to him, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.’
verses.after: Judah answered, “The man warned us plainly: ‘You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But Judah said to him, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.’

verses.rationale: Retains the direct condition and Judah’s promise to procure food for Jacob.
verses.before: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
verses.after: If you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.

verses.rationale: Repeats the warning verbatim because its force is central to the argument.
verses.before: But if you will not send him, we will not go down, for the man said to us, ‘You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.’”
verses.after: But if you will not send him, we will not go. The man told us, ‘You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you will not send him, we will not go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the name Israel and the father’s accusation rather than softening it into a neutral request for information.
verses.before: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly as to tell the man that you had another brother?”
verses.after: Israel said, “Why did you bring this trouble on me by telling the man you had another brother?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly as to tell the man that you had another brother?”

verses.rationale: Preserves questions reported here but not narrated in the first exchange, without rewriting that earlier scene to match.
verses.before: They said, “The man questioned us carefully about ourselves and our family, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ We answered according to these words. How could we know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”
verses.after: They answered, “The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family: ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ We answered his questions. How could we have known he would tell us to bring our brother down?”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “The man questioned us carefully about ourselves and our family, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ We answered according to these words. How could we know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”

verses.rationale: Retains the live/not-die formula and names all three groups whose survival depends on the journey.
verses.before: Then Judah said to Israel his father, “Send the boy with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live and not die, both we and you and also our little ones.
verses.after: Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the young man with me, and let us be on our way, so we can live and not die—we, you, and our little ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Judah said to Israel his father, “Send the boy with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live and not die, both we and you and also our little ones.

verses.rationale: Makes Judah’s personal surety clear without transferring risk to someone else as Reuben did.
verses.before: I myself will be surety for him. From my hand you may require him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him before you, then let me bear the blame before you forever.
verses.after: I myself will guarantee his safety. You can hold me responsible for him. If I do not bring him back and stand him before you, I will bear the blame before you all my life.
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself will be surety for him. From my hand you may require him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him before you, then let me bear the blame before you forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps the counterfactual complaint and exact twice emphasis.
verses.before: For if we had not delayed, surely by now we could have returned twice.”
verses.after: If we had not delayed, we could have been back twice by now.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For if we had not delayed, surely by now we could have returned twice.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all six gift items and their relation to the land despite the grain famine; repeats 37:25’s cargo terms.
verses.before: Then Israel their father said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: take some of the best products of the land in your bags and carry down to the man a gift—a little balm and a little honey, gum, myrrh, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
verses.after: Then their father Israel said, “If it must be so, do this. Put some of the land’s finest produce in your bags and take the man a gift: a little balm and honey, gum and resin, pistachios and almonds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Israel their father said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: take some of the best products of the land in your bags and carry down to the man a gift—a little balm and a little honey, gum, myrrh, pistachio nuts, and almonds.

verses.rationale: Retains double silver alongside returned silver without deciding whether the returned money is included in the double amount.
verses.before: Take double the silver with you. Carry back with you the silver that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.
verses.after: Take twice as much silver with you, and return the silver that was put back at the mouths of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take double the silver with you. Carry back with you the silver that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jacob’s practical authorization after his earlier refusal.
verses.before: Take your brother also, and arise, return to the man.
verses.after: Take your brother too, and go back to the man.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take your brother also, and arise, return to the man.

verses.rationale: Retains El Shaddai’s established rendering, compassion, the unnamed other brother, and the repeated resigned bereavement formula.
verses.before: May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, so that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. And as for me, if I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”
verses.after: May God Almighty grant you compassion before the man, so he releases your other brother and Benjamin to you. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, so that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. And as for me, if I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the full three-part provision and movement into Joseph’s presence.
verses.before: So the men took this gift, and they took double the silver with them, and Benjamin. They arose and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
verses.after: The men took the gift, twice the silver, and Benjamin. They set out for Egypt and presented themselves before Joseph.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the men took this gift, and they took double the silver with them, and Benjamin. They arose and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

verses.rationale: Identifies the household official by function and preserves slaughter, preparation, and exact mealtime.
verses.before: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, slaughter an animal, and prepare it, for the men are to eat with me at noon.”
verses.after: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he told his household steward, “Bring these men into the house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they will eat with me at noon.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, slaughter an animal, and prepare it, for the men are to eat with me at noon.”

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit fulfillment of Joseph’s order and its destination.
verses.before: The man did as Joseph said and brought the men into Joseph’s house.
verses.after: The steward did as Joseph said and brought the men to Joseph’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The man did as Joseph said and brought the men into Joseph’s house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the brothers’ feared attack, enslavement, and confiscation as their interpretation, not Joseph’s stated intention.
verses.before: And the men were afraid because they were brought into Joseph’s house. They said, “It is because of the silver that was returned in our sacks the first time that we are brought in, so that he may seek an occasion against us and fall upon us and take us as slaves along with our donkeys.”
verses.after: The men were afraid because they were being brought to Joseph’s house. “It is because of the silver returned to our sacks the first time,” they said. “He means to find a charge against us, fall upon us, and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the men were afraid because they were brought into Joseph’s house. They said, “It is because of the silver that was returned in our sacks the first time that we are brought in, so that he may seek an occasion against us and fall upon us and take us as slaves along with our donkeys.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the threshold setting before they enter as guests.
verses.before: So they came near to the steward of Joseph’s house and spoke with him at the entrance of the house,
verses.after: At the entrance to Joseph’s house, they approached his steward and spoke to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they came near to the steward of Joseph’s house and spoke with him at the entrance of the house,

verses.rationale: Preserves deferential address and the reiterated purpose of the earlier journey.
verses.before: saying, “Please, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.
verses.after: “Please, my lord,” they said, “we came down the first time to buy food.
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “Please, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.

verses.rationale: Keeps their collective account of discovery and silver by weight, without correcting it to the earlier narrator’s sequence.
verses.before: And when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, look, each man’s silver was in the mouth of his sack, our silver in full weight. So we have brought it back with us.
verses.after: When we reached our lodging place and opened our sacks, each man’s silver was there at the mouth of his sack—the full weight of it. We have brought it back with us.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, behold, each man’s silver was in the mouth of his sack, our silver in full weight. So we have brought it back with us.

verses.rationale: Preserves their attempted restitution and truthful lack of knowledge about Joseph’s orders.
verses.before: We have also brought down with us additional silver to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”
verses.after: We have brought more silver to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”
verses.tsw_comparator: We have also brought down with us additional silver to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”

verses.rationale: Retains shalom, the steward’s attribution to their ancestral God, his receipt claim, and Simeon’s release without inventing how the accounts balance.
verses.before: He said, “Peace to you. Do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has put treasure in your sacks for you. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.after: “Peace to you. Do not be afraid,” he said. “Your God, the God of your father, gave you treasure in your sacks. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Peace to you. Do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has put treasure in your sacks for you. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps hospitality to both travelers and their animals and explicitly states the men’s completed footwashing.
verses.before: And the man brought the men into Joseph’s house and gave them water, and they washed their feet. And he gave their donkeys fodder.
verses.after: The steward brought the men into Joseph’s house and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He also supplied feed for their donkeys.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the man brought the men into Joseph’s house and gave them water, and they washed their feet. And he gave their donkeys fodder.

verses.rationale: Retains the gift preparation and the reason for expecting a shared meal.
verses.before: So they prepared the gift for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they would eat bread there.
verses.after: They arranged their gift for Joseph’s arrival at noon, because they had heard they would eat there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they prepared the gift for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they would eat bread there.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated gift and bow, continuing the dream imagery.
verses.before: When Joseph came home, they brought into the house to him the gift that they had with them and bowed down to him to the ground.
verses.after: When Joseph came home, they brought their gift into the house and bowed to the ground before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joseph came home, they brought into the house to him the gift that they had with them and bowed down to him to the ground.

verses.rationale: Renders the shalom inquiries naturally while keeping both welfare and survival questions.
verses.before: And he asked them about their welfare and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?”
verses.after: He asked how they were doing, then said, “Is your elderly father well, the one you told me about? Is he still alive?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he asked them about their welfare and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?”

verses.rationale: Follows the source’s written/read form for bowing and preserves both gestures and the deferential description of Jacob.
verses.before: They said, “Your servant our father is well. He is still alive.” And they bowed their heads and paid homage.
verses.after: “Your servant our father is well,” they answered. “He is still alive.” They bowed low and prostrated themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “Your servant our father is well. He is still alive.” And they bowed their heads and paid homage.

verses.rationale: Makes the full-brother relationship explicit and retains my son as Joseph’s affectionate address, not literal parentage.
verses.before: Then he lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” And he said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
verses.after: Joseph looked up and saw Benjamin, his brother, his own mother’s son. “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” he asked. Then he said, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” And he said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”

verses.rationale: Connects his stirring compassion to Jacob’s prayer using the same root, without suppressing emotion or prematurely revealing his identity.
verses.before: Then Joseph hurried out, for his compassion grew warm for his brother, and he sought a place to weep. And he entered his chamber and wept there.
verses.after: Overcome with compassion for his brother, Joseph hurried away to find a place to weep. He went into a private room and wept there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joseph hurried out, for his compassion grew warm for his brother, and he sought a place to weep. And he entered his chamber and wept there.

verses.rationale: Preserves self-restraint after private weeping and the command to serve.
verses.before: Then he washed his face and came out. And controlling himself, he said, “Serve the meal.”
verses.after: He washed his face and came out. Regaining his composure, he said, “Serve the food.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he washed his face and came out. And controlling himself, he said, “Serve the meal.”

verses.rationale: Keeps three dining groups and attributes the strong taboo judgment to the Egyptians without supplying an unverified historical explanation.
verses.before: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that was an abomination to the Egyptians.
verses.after: Joseph was served separately, his brothers separately, and the Egyptians who ate with him separately. Egyptians would not eat with Hebrews, because they considered it an abomination.
verses.tsw_comparator: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that was an abomination to the Egyptians.

verses.rationale: Preserves ordered seating and their reaction without claiming how the order was arranged.
verses.before: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth. And the men looked at one another in amazement.
verses.after: The brothers were seated before him in order of age, from the firstborn to the youngest. They looked at one another in amazement.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth. And the men looked at one another in amazement.

verses.rationale: Keeps favoritism’s exact ratio and the intoxication verb rather than reducing it to general merriment.
verses.before: Portions were taken to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times greater than any of theirs. And they drank and were merry with him.
verses.after: Portions were sent to them from Joseph’s table, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as large as anyone else’s. They drank with Joseph and became drunk.
verses.tsw_comparator: Portions were taken to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times greater than any of theirs. And they drank and were merry with him.

verses.rationale: Makes Joseph the explicit subject and retains capacity-limited provisioning and returned silver.
verses.before: Then he commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.
verses.after: Joseph instructed his household steward, “Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each man’s silver at the mouth of his sack.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.

verses.rationale: Preserves the planted evidence, emphatic silver-cup identification, and fulfillment that establish the accusation’s falsity.
verses.before: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, along with the silver for his grain.” And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
verses.after: Put my cup—the silver cup—at the mouth of the youngest brother’s sack, along with the silver for his grain.” The steward did just as Joseph said.
verses.tsw_comparator: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, along with the silver for his grain.” And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

verses.rationale: Keeps dawn departure and their transport animals without adding a destination.
verses.before: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away with their donkeys.
verses.after: At daybreak the men were sent off with their donkeys.
verses.tsw_comparator: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away with their donkeys.

verses.rationale: Retains short distance, urgency, nested speech, and the good/evil accusation.
verses.before: They had gone only a short distance from the city and had not yet gone far when Joseph said to his steward, “Rise, pursue the men, and when you overtake them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good?
verses.after: They had left the city but had not gone far when Joseph told his steward, “Go after those men at once. When you catch up with them, say, ‘Why have you repaid good with evil?
verses.tsw_comparator: They had gone only a short distance from the city and had not yet gone far when Joseph said to his steward, “Rise, pursue the men, and when you overtake them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good?

verses.rationale: Keeps the claim of divination in the instructed speech without endorsing or denying Joseph’s actual practice.
verses.before: Is not this the cup from which my lord drinks and by which he indeed practices divination? You have done evil in doing this.’”
verses.after: Isn’t this the cup my master drinks from and uses for divination? What you have done is evil!’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not this the cup from which my lord drinks and by which he indeed practices divination? You have done evil in doing this.’”

verses.rationale: Identifies the pursuer and preserves his exact reporting role.
verses.before: When he overtook them, he spoke these words to them.
verses.after: The steward caught up with them and repeated these words.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he overtook them, he spoke these words to them.

verses.rationale: Uses a natural emphatic denial while keeping the servants’ deferential stance.
verses.before: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing.
verses.after: They answered, “Why does my lord say such things? Your servants would never do anything like that!
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing.

verses.rationale: Preserves the argument from returned silver and both precious metals.
verses.before: Look, the silver that we found in the mouths of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord’s house?
verses.after: We brought back from Canaan the silver we found at the mouths of our sacks. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, the silver that we found in the mouths of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord’s house?

verses.rationale: Keeps the rash death pledge and collective enslavement without softening their proposed penalty.
verses.before: Whichever of your servants is found with it will die, and we also will become my lord’s slaves.”
verses.after: If the cup is found with any of your servants, let that man die, and the rest of us will become my lord’s slaves.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whichever of your servants is found with it shall die, and we also will become my lord’s slaves.”

verses.rationale: Retains the source’s apparent assent followed by a changed penalty; the discrepancy is disclosed rather than silently repaired.
verses.before: He said, “Let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found will become my slave, and the rest of you will be innocent.”
verses.after: He replied, “Very well, let it be as you say: whoever is found with the cup will become my slave, and the rest of you will be free of blame.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found shall become my slave, and the rest of you shall be innocent.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated each-man action and readiness to submit to the search.
verses.before: Then each man quickly lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
verses.after: Each man hurried to lower his sack to the ground and open it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then each man quickly lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.

verses.rationale: Preserves the deliberate age sequence and passive discovery after the known planting.
verses.before: And he searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
verses.after: The steward searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

verses.rationale: Keeps the collective grief and collective return rather than implying they abandon Benjamin.
verses.before: Then they tore their garments. And every man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
verses.after: They tore their clothes. Then each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they tore their garments. And every man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah’s prominence in the group and the repeated prostration.
verses.before: When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, he was still there. And they fell before him to the ground.
verses.after: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, where Joseph still was, and fell to the ground before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, he was still there. And they fell before him to the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains the emphatic claim as Joseph’s speech without substituting ordinary investigative skill.
verses.before: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Do you not know that a man like me can indeed practice divination?”
verses.after: Joseph said, “What is this you have done? Didn’t you know that a man like me can certainly practice divination?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Do you not know that a man like me can indeed practice divination?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the three questions, attributed divine exposure, and solidarity; guilt is not forced into an admission of cup theft.
verses.before: Judah said, “What will we say to my lord? What will we speak? And how will we clear ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants. Look, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup has been found.”
verses.after: Judah answered, “What can we say to my lord? What can we tell you? How can we prove ourselves innocent? God has uncovered your servants’ guilt. Here we are, my lord’s slaves—all of us, along with the one who had the cup.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah said, “What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? And how shall we clear ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup has been found.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Joseph’s restricted sentence and ironic offer of peace while leaving Benjamin enslaved.
verses.before: But he said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. Only the man in whose hand the cup was found will be my slave. But as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
verses.after: Joseph said, “I would never do that. Only the man who had the cup will become my slave. The rest of you may go up to your father in peace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. Only the man in whose hand the cup was found shall be my slave. But as for you, go up in peace to your father.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Judah’s approach, deference, fear of anger, and comparison to Pharaoh without asserting identical royal rank.
verses.before: Then Judah came near to him and said, “Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and let not your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself.
verses.after: Judah stepped forward. “Please, my lord,” he said, “let your servant speak a word in your hearing. Do not be angry with your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Judah came near to him and said, “Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and let not your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah’s version of the initial questioning without harmonizing it with chapter 42.
verses.before: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father or a brother?’
verses.after: My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
verses.tsw_comparator: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father or a brother?’

verses.rationale: Clarifies the son’s relationship to the speakers and the shared mother while retaining the explicit death report in Judah’s retelling.
verses.before: And we said to my lord, ‘We have an aged father and a young child of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone remains of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’
verses.after: We told my lord, ‘We have an elderly father, and our youngest brother was born to him in his old age. His full brother is dead. He alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And we said to my lord, ‘We have an aged father and a young child of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone remains of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the eye idiom without deciding whether it means simply seeing or protective attention.
verses.before: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes upon him.’
verses.after: You told your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so I can set my eyes on him.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes upon him.’

verses.rationale: Names the likely subject of die in light of 44:30–31, while a note acknowledges the grammatically possible son reading.
verses.before: But we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
verses.after: We said to my lord, ‘The young man cannot leave his father. If he leaves, his father will die.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’

verses.rationale: Retains the condition and repeated face language as Judah frames the impasse.
verses.before: Then you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’
verses.after: But you told your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not see my face again.’

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah’s deference toward Joseph even while speaking of his own father.
verses.before: When we went back to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
verses.after: When we went back to your servant my father, we told him what my lord had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: When we went back to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

verses.rationale: Retains the direct repeated request from 43:2 rather than reducing the speech to a summary.
verses.before: And when our father said, ‘Go again, buy us a little food,’
verses.after: Then our father said, ‘Go back and buy us a little food.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And when our father said, ‘Go again, buy us a little food,’

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated conditions and face formula while using natural clause order.
verses.before: we said, ‘We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down, for we cannot see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
verses.after: We answered, ‘We cannot go down unless our youngest brother is with us. If he comes, we will go, because we cannot see the man’s face without our youngest brother.’
verses.tsw_comparator: we said, ‘We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down, for we cannot see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’

verses.rationale: Preserves Jacob’s own selective my-wife/two-sons wording rather than correcting it to his whole household.
verses.before: Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
verses.after: Your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jacob’s inference as reported speech and the emphatic torn-to-pieces expression.
verses.before: One left me, and I said, “Surely he has been torn to pieces,” and I have not seen him since.
verses.after: One left me, and I said he must surely have been torn to pieces. I have not seen him since.
verses.tsw_comparator: One left me, and I said, “Surely he has been torn to pieces,” and I have not seen him since.

verses.rationale: Retains disaster, gray head, Sheol, and the distinct misery term rather than flattening every grief formula.
verses.before: If you take this one also from me, and harm befalls him, you will bring down my gray hair in misery to Sheol.’
verses.after: If you take this one from me too and disaster strikes him, you will bring my gray head down to Sheol in misery.’
verses.tsw_comparator: If you take this one also from me, and harm befalls him, you will bring down my gray hair in misery to Sheol.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the bound-lives image and sentence suspension while explicitly naming both life referents.
verses.before: Now therefore, when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us, since his life is bound up in the boy’s life,
verses.after: So now, when I return to your servant my father without the young man—my father’s life is bound to the young man’s life—
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us, since his life is bound up in the boy’s life,

verses.rationale: Completes the suspended sentence and preserves Judah’s repeated deference and feared responsibility for Jacob’s death.
verses.before: when he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. And your servants will bring down the gray hair of your servant our father with sorrow to Sheol.
verses.after: he will die when he sees that the young man is not with us. Your servants will bring the gray head of your servant our father down to Sheol in grief.
verses.tsw_comparator: when he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. And your servants will bring down the gray hair of your servant our father with sorrow to Sheol.

verses.rationale: Recalls Judah’s personal guarantee in 43:9, preserving permanent accountability rather than financial compensation.
verses.before: For your servant became surety for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then I will bear the blame before my father all my days.’
verses.after: Your servant guaranteed the young man’s safety to my father. I told him, ‘If I do not bring him back, I will bear the blame before my father all my life.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For your servant became surety for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then I shall bear the blame before my father all my days.’

verses.rationale: Makes the substitution and actual enslavement explicit; servants as court politeness remains distinct from slave as penalty.
verses.before: Now therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
verses.after: Now, please let your servant stay as my lord’s slave in the young man’s place, and let the young man go back with his brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah’s final question and focus on his father’s suffering rather than resolving Joseph’s response in advance.
verses.before: For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? I fear to see the evil that would come upon my father.”
verses.after: How can I go back to my father without the young man? I cannot bear to see the suffering that would overtake my father.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? I fear to see the evil that would come upon my father.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the loss of restraint and privacy for disclosure while clarifying that the brothers remain.
verses.before: Then Joseph could not restrain himself before all people who stood by him. He cried, “Send everyone out from me.” So no one stayed with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
verses.after: Joseph could no longer hold himself back in front of all his attendants. “Have everyone leave me!” he cried. No one else was with him when he made himself known to his brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joseph could not restrain himself before all those who stood by him. He cried, “Send everyone out from me.” So no one stayed with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

verses.rationale: Preserves both circles reached by the weeping without requiring Pharaoh’s distant household to hear the sound itself.
verses.before: And he wept aloud, so that the Egyptians heard it, and the household of Pharaoh heard it.
verses.after: He wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh’s household heard about it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he wept aloud, so that the Egyptians heard it, and the household of Pharaoh heard it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed father question despite their previous answer and preserves terror rather than merely surprise.
verses.before: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?” But his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed at his presence.
verses.after: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” His brothers could not answer him; they were terrified in his presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?” But his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed at his presence.

verses.rationale: Retains brotherhood and explicit responsibility for the sale in Joseph’s own words.
verses.before: So Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” And they came near. And he said, “I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.after: “Please come closer,” Joseph said. They came closer, and he said, “I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” And they came near. And he said, “I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps Joseph’s interpretation of divine purpose alongside the named human sale, without supplying a general rule about suffering.
verses.before: And now do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
verses.after: Do not be distressed or angry with yourselves for selling me here, because God sent me ahead of you to preserve life.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact elapsed and remaining periods and both agricultural activities.
verses.before: For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are yet five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
verses.after: The famine has been in the land for two years, and five more years remain without plowing or harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are yet five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.

verses.rationale: Keeps remnant and deliverance as consequential biblical terms while noting the alternative many-survivors sense.
verses.before: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on earth, and to keep alive for you many survivors.
verses.after: God sent me ahead of you to preserve a remnant for you on the earth and to keep you alive through a great deliverance.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on earth, and to keep alive for you many survivors.

verses.rationale: Preserves Joseph’s strong human/divine contrast and the father-to-Pharaoh metaphor rather than replacing it with a job title.
verses.before: So it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
verses.after: So it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of his whole household, and ruler over all Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: So it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps urgency, the message formula, and Joseph’s attribution of authority to God.
verses.before: Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, ‘Thus says your son Joseph, God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.
verses.after: Hurry back to my father and tell him, ‘Your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me without delay.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, ‘Thus says your son Joseph, God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.

verses.rationale: Preserves three generations, both livestock groups, all possessions, and proximity to Joseph.
verses.before: You will dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near me, you and your children and your children’s children, and your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
verses.after: You can settle in Goshen and be near me—you, your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you have.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me, you and your children and your children’s children, and your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.

verses.rationale: Keeps Joseph’s support and the stated danger of impoverishment, rather than changing it to immediate starvation.
verses.before: There I will provide for you, for there are yet five years of famine to come, so that you and your household, and all that you have, do not come to poverty.’
verses.after: I will provide for you there, for five years of famine remain. Otherwise you, your household, and all you have will fall into poverty.’
verses.tsw_comparator: There I will provide for you, for there are yet five years of famine to come, so that you and your household, and all that you have, do not come to poverty.’

verses.rationale: Retains the mouth-and-eyes language of direct recognition without inserting an unspoken claim about which language Joseph uses.
verses.before: And now your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
verses.after: You can see for yourselves, and my brother Benjamin can see, that it is my own mouth speaking to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps reported honor, eyewitness testimony, and the repeated urgency to reunite with his father.
verses.before: You must tell my father of all my honor in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.”
verses.after: Tell my father about all the honor I have in Egypt and everything you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You must tell my father of all my honor in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the bodily neck image and reciprocal tears rather than reducing the encounter to generic affection.
verses.before: Then he fell upon his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
verses.after: Then he threw his arms around his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he fell upon his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.

verses.rationale: Keeps all brothers included and speech’s delayed return without inventing what they said or claiming the relationship is fully repaired.
verses.before: And he kissed all his brothers and wept upon them. After that his brothers talked with him.
verses.after: He kissed all his brothers and wept over them. After that, his brothers spoke with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he kissed all his brothers and wept upon them. After that his brothers talked with him.

verses.rationale: Retains the report’s spread and the positive royal-household response.
verses.before: When the report was heard in Pharaoh’s house, “Joseph’s brothers have come,” it pleased Pharaoh and his servants.
verses.after: Word reached Pharaoh’s household that Joseph’s brothers had come. Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the report was heard in Pharaoh’s house, “Joseph’s brothers have come,” it pleased Pharaoh and his servants.

verses.rationale: Keeps Pharaoh’s instructions as a message relayed through Joseph.
verses.before: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: load your beasts and go back to the land of Canaan,
verses.after: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: load your animals and return to Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: load your beasts and go back to the land of Canaan,

verses.rationale: Preserves the rich fat-of-the-land image and Pharaoh’s offer to the whole family.
verses.before: and take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’
verses.after: Bring your father and your households back to me. I will give you the best of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’
verses.tsw_comparator: and take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.’

verses.rationale: Clarifies the switch from singular Joseph to plural brothers while retaining command, wagons, children, wives, and father.
verses.before: And you, Joseph, are commanded to say, ‘Do this: take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
verses.after: You are also instructed to tell them, ‘Do this: take wagons from Egypt for your little ones and your wives, bring your father, and come.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, Joseph, are commanded to say, ‘Do this: take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.

verses.rationale: Renders the eye-not-pity idiom as practical reassurance about possessions, keeping the royal promise.
verses.before: Have no concern for your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’”
verses.after: Do not worry about your belongings, because the best of all Egypt will be yours.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Have no concern for your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the Israel designation, obedience, wagons, and journey supplies.
verses.before: The sons of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons, according to the command of Pharaoh, and gave them provisions for the journey.
verses.after: Israel’s sons did as they were told. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had ordered and provisions for the journey.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons, according to the command of Pharaoh, and gave them provisions for the journey.

verses.rationale: Preserves renewed preferential treatment, exact silver amount, and five clothing sets without equating silver pieces with minted coins.
verses.before: To each and all of them he gave a change of garments, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments.
verses.after: He gave each of them a change of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: To each and all of them he gave a change of garments, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments.

verses.rationale: Retains the sex distinction, both tens, and the threefold provisioning list.
verses.before: To his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and provision for his father on the journey.
verses.after: He sent his father ten male donkeys carrying the finest things from Egypt and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and other food for his father’s journey.
verses.tsw_comparator: To his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and provision for his father on the journey.

verses.rationale: Chooses the contextual quarrel sense of a verb that can also mean be agitated or afraid, with the alternative noted.
verses.before: Then he sent his brothers away, and as they departed he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way.”
verses.after: He sent his brothers on their way and said to them, “Do not quarrel on the journey.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he sent his brothers away, and as they departed he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the up-from-Egypt movement, destination, and reunion with Jacob.
verses.before: So they went up out of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan to their father Jacob.
verses.after: They went up from Egypt and came to their father Jacob in Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they went up out of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan to their father Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sudden news and bodily heart response without inventing a medical event.
verses.before: And they told him, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” And his heart became numb, for he did not believe them.
verses.after: “Joseph is still alive!” they told him. “He is ruler over all Egypt!” But Jacob’s heart went numb; he did not believe them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they told him, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” And his heart became numb, for he did not believe them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the combined words-and-visible-wagons evidence and the spirit’s revival.
verses.before: But when they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.
verses.after: They told him everything Joseph had said. When Jacob saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, their father’s spirit revived.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.

verses.rationale: Preserves the name switch to Israel, his abrupt enough, and life/death framing at the reunion’s threshold.
verses.before: Israel said, “It is enough; Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”
verses.after: Israel said, “That is enough! My son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Israel said, “It is enough; Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

comparative_references.scope: Every verse in Genesis 42–45; read after the independent Hebrew draft.
Secondary comparison for silver, hospitality, and the final drinking verb; consulted after Hebrew drafting.

comparative_references.source: NET translators’ notes, Biblical Studies Press
comparative_references.scope: Secondary grammatical comparison for divination, changed penalty, father/son pronouns, and gray-head language; source interpretation remains editorially pending.
